tasks.short: Process supplier invoices and release the payment batch.

today.trigger: Invoices arrive daily by mail, from carriers, and from the three staffing-agency portals, and due dates fall on the Rabobank payment run.
steps: Collect PDFs and portal invoices from Outlook, SharePoint and the agency portals into AFAS Profit.
Code each invoice to a grootboekrekening, btw-code and kostenplaats, and match it to a purchase order or receipt where one exists.
Chase missing receipts, disputed flex hours and price differences with the bookkeepers or the agency.
Build the payment proposal in AFAS for invoices that are approved and due.
Export a SEPA batch and have a second authorised person release it in Rabobank.
drudgery: Re-typing invoice headers and VAT lines that a file already contains
Opening three agency portals to copy the same hours into AFAS
Holding a complete batch because one line is missing a receipt
today.time_sinks: Most of the 134 hours per accountant per year sits in coding, portal re-keying and exception chasing, not in the Rabobank release itself.

lenses.faster: Matched invoices are coded and proposed for payment without a person retyping them. The accountant only opens lines that fail a match, a VAT check or a duplicate check.
lenses.autonomous: A new e-invoice, mailbox PDF or agency file starts the match on arrival. The payment run is created on the agreed Rabobank day, not when someone remembers.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would post carrier and flex-worker cost to Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo in the week the work happened, so the forecast is not waiting for a lump invoice.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses copying portal lines into AFAS. What remains is the argument about a real price or hours dispute.
lenses.options: The accountant sees the batch under three cuts: pay all matched items, hold items over a Controller-set amount, and hold every new supplier.
lenses.altitude: The accountant maintains supplier rules, VAT defaults and the match tolerances, and reviews the exceptions, rather than coding each invoice.
reach: Straight-through coding now done by the bookkeepers on purchase invoices
Cash application of customer receipts, shared with the credit and collections officer
The payroll control-account side of agency invoices, shared with the payroll specialist

tasks.human_edge: Judgment when a flex-hour invoice does not match the ordered shifts, and the decision to release company money.
tasks.pattern_why: Capture, matching and the payment proposal can run as steps across AFAS, the mailbox and the agency files, but a SEPA batch must not count until a second person releases it.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice file lands in the AFAS purchase queue, or the payment calendar reaches the Rabobank run.
steps: Read the invoice into header, lines, IBAN, VAT and site from UBL or PDF, and from a line file where the agency provides one.
Match supplier, purchase order, receipt and amount. Apply the supplier's btw-code only when the line does not contradict it.
Park duplicates, new IBANs, VAT clashes and unmatched lines for the accountant, with the source file attached.
Build the payment proposal from due invoices that passed the match.
A second authorised person releases the SEPA batch to Rabobank.
in_practice.human_gate: No batch is sent to Rabobank without a named second person releasing it. New VAT treatments, new IBANs and unmatched invoices above the Controller's limit wait for the accountant.
systems: AFAS Profit accounts payable and workflow
data_needed: Supplier master with IBAN, default account, btw-code and kostenplaats
Open purchase orders and receipts in AFAS
Agency line files with hours, rate, site and invoice number
The Rabobank mandate and the AFAS authorisation matrix
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS posting and workflow log, plus the released pain.001 file stored in the finance SharePoint close folder.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit registers purchase invoices, routes them through workflow and creates SEPA payment proposals.
Rabobank business banking accepts SEPA bulk payment files from accounting software.
Dutch invoice-capture products such as Basecone and Klippa read header and line fields from PDF invoices.
A stable agency hour file can be matched to site cost without a model.

risks: A wrong btw-code on international transport (zero rate or verleggingsregeling) creates a VAT error the Belastingdienst will still charge to Noordhaven.
Auto-paying a changed IBAN or a duplicate PDF is a fraud and segregation-of-duties failure.
Agency invoices name flex workers. Storing those names in an AI tool outside AFAS needs an AVG purpose and a processor agreement.
If most invoices have no purchase order, the queue of exceptions is as long as today's work.
research_questions: What share of last quarter's invoices had a purchase order and a receipt in AFAS before the invoice arrived, split by carriers, agencies and other suppliers?
Can each of the three agencies deliver a line file with hours, rate, site and invoice number, or only a PDF?
What do the AFAS authorisation scheme and the Rabobank mandate require before a batch can be released, and will the auditor accept auto-coding when the supplier rule is stored on the posting?
How many logistics invoices use a VAT treatment that is not the supplier default?

tasks.short: Check the books and prepare the monthly figures.

today.trigger: Month-end close, a request from the Finance Director, or a question on the Power BI pack that does not match what people expected.
steps: Export trial balance, subledgers and VAT boxes from AFAS Profit.
Tie debtors, creditors, bank, payroll and VAT to the general ledger in Excel.
Check the mapping into the monthly profit and loss and balance sheet, including the three sites.
Compare with last month and with the forecast, and look for missing accruals or cut-off errors.
Send the pack to the Controller and explain the lines that moved.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same Excel bridge every month
Hunting rounding differences between AFAS and Power BI
Copying last month's commentary forward
today.time_sinks: The slow part is tying subledgers and explaining shifts in warehouse and transport margin, especially the flex-labour swing of 150 to 300 workers.

lenses.faster: The trial balance, subledger ties and the standard monthly pack are produced from AFAS when the period is locked. The accountant starts at the breaks and the margin moves.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS extract refreshes a check pack. A broken tie or a flux over the threshold opens a task before the close meeting.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the sites would get a weekly profit and loss they can use while the month is still open, with shipment cut-off shown separately.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rebuilding pivots and chasing cents. The work people want is deciding whether a margin move is real.
lenses.options: Five presentations of the same close sit side by side: with and without flex accrual, with and without late POD cut-off, and against the forecast the business already saw.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the check catalogue, the account mapping and the flux thresholds, and reviews what fails.
reach: First draft of the Controller's management pack
The actuals bridge the FP&A analysts now rebuild
Subledger tie-out the bookkeepers prepare for close

tasks.human_edge: Judgment on whether the figures are complete enough to show the business, including loads that left a site but have no proof of delivery yet.
tasks.pattern_why: Ties, mappings and flux checks are repeatable and checkable, but the monthly figures do not count as Noordhaven's result until the accountant signs them.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS period lock starts, or the nightly extract shows a tie or flux break.
steps: Pull the trial balance and the debtors, creditors, bank, VAT and payroll subledgers from AFAS, not from a copied Excel file.
Run the tie list, the mapping to the monthly statements and the flux against last month and the forecast.
Draft the site profit and loss for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo with the open breaks listed.
The accountant accepts or rejects each break and writes the commentary that is still open.
The signed pack is stored for the Controller and the Finance Director.
in_practice.human_gate: The pack is not the official month until the accountant signs it. The Controller still owns anything that goes to the bank, the shareholder or the Kamer van Koophandel.
data_needed: Locked AFAS trial balance and subledgers
The mapping from grootboek to the management pack and to Dutch GAAP headings
Forecast version the business is using
Site cut-off status for transport orders and warehouse shipments
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint close folder: the check result, the sign-off and the AFAS period used.

evidence.claim: Silverfin and CaseWare build a tied statement pack from a trial balance and a mapping.
The company already refreshes Power BI from a nightly AFAS extract, so a check pack can be scheduled on that extract.
A Dutch BV of this size typically reports under BW2 Title 9 and the Raad voor de Jaarverslaggeving, and files via SBR.

risks: Power BI is a night behind AFAS. Closing from the dashboard alone will not match the ledger on close day.
An automated pack can look complete while Venlo cut-off is still open.
Commentary written by a model can invent a cause for a margin move. The accountant must only publish causes that tie to a document.
Statutory presentation is a professional judgment. A wrong RJ mapping is an audit adjustment, which is one of the team's input metrics.
research_questions: Is today's monthly pack built from the AFAS trial balance, or from Excel files that are adjusted after export?
Which rules apply, Dutch GAAP only or also a group IFRS pack, and who signs each?
On what day do the three sites freeze proof-of-delivery and warehouse completion, and how often does that date slip?
What share of these 97 hours is tie-out, and what share is explaining the result?

tasks.short: Reconcile the accounts and clear the differences.

today.trigger: Month-end, a Rabobank statement import, or an account that does not match its subledger (bank, VAT, payroll, debtors, creditors, agency cost).
steps: Import the Rabobank statement into AFAS and match lines to open invoices and payments.
Export what did not match to Excel.
Clear payroll, VAT and inter-site differences against the journals of that month.
Ask bookkeepers, payroll or an agency about the lines that remain.
Sign the reconciliation and carry the open items into next month.
drudgery: Matching lines that already share amount, date and invoice number
Copying the same open item into a new workbook each month
Chasing a difference that is a timing gap already explained last month
today.time_sinks: The hours sit in unmatched bank lines, agency payments that cover several invoices, and clearing accounts that are only looked at on close day.

lenses.faster: Amount, date and reference matches clear themselves when the statement lands. The accountant works the unmatched list only.
lenses.autonomous: Each Rabobank import and each AFAS night run refreshes the reconciliation. An item older than the agreed days opens a task without a reminder.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, cash and days sales outstanding would be reliable every morning, and agency cost by site would be reconciled every week.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses ticking matched lines. What remains is tracing a real missing payment or a mis-posted site.
lenses.options: The same bank line is shown against the top few open invoices it might settle, with the match key visible, so the accountant picks rather than searches.
lenses.altitude: The accountant sets the match keys, the tolerance and the ageing limit, and reviews breaks and the monthly sign-off.
reach: Customer cash application now done with the credit and collections officer
The payroll clearing tie-out now done with the payroll specialist
Creditor statement checks now done by the bookkeepers

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what an unmatched line really is when the reference is missing, and whether the account is fair to sign.
tasks.pattern_why: Bank lines, open items and clearing balances are structured. Match rules can be written down and the result can be checked without a model in the path.

in_practice.trigger: A Rabobank CAMT or MT940 file is imported, or the nightly AFAS run finds a subledger that does not tie.
steps: Match bank lines to open items on amount, invoice number, IBAN and date window.
Auto-clear matches inside the tolerance the Controller has set.
Group leftover agency payments that cover several invoices and propose the split from the remittance reference.
List open items older than the limit, with the last explanation attached.
The accountant signs the account once the open list is accepted.
in_practice.human_gate: An account is not reconciled until the accountant signs the open-item list. Auto-cleared lines are not approved one by one. Anything outside tolerance, or without a reference, waits.
systems: AFAS Profit bank and general ledger
data_needed: CAMT.053 or MT940 from Rabobank
Open debtors, creditors and clearing accounts in AFAS
Supplier and customer IBANs
Documented tolerance and ageing limits
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS match log and a signed reconciliation PDF in the SharePoint close folder.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit imports bank statements and proposes matches to open items.
Rabobank delivers CAMT.053 and MT940 statements to business customers.
BlackLine matches ledger lines and stores a reconciliation sign-off.

risks: A tolerance that is too wide will clear the wrong invoice and hide a real cash difference.
Agency payments often arrive as one net amount. A rules engine that expects one invoice per line will leave the hard part, which is where the hours already are.
Auto-clearing without a stored match key will be rejected by the auditor and come back as an audit adjustment.
Customer remittance data that contains personal names must stay in AFAS and not in a separate tool without an AVG check.
research_questions: What percentage of Rabobank lines auto-match in AFAS today, and which statement format is imported?
How many euros sit on bank, VAT, payroll clearing and agency cost, and how old are the open items?
How often do customer receipts contain an invoice number that AFAS can read?
Will the auditor accept auto-cleared matches below a written tolerance without re-performing every line?

tasks.short: Check that the bookkeeping follows the agreed procedures.

today.trigger: A close review, an auditor request, a new AFAS user, or a suspicion that postings are bypassing the process.
steps: Read the procedure notes on SharePoint and the AFAS authorisation matrix.
Sample journals, invoices and master-data changes.
Check whether the same person created and approved a payment, or posted after the period lock.
Write findings and agree actions with the Controller.
File the sample for the external auditor.
drudgery: Asking bookkeepers for screenshots the audit log already has
Rebuilding the authorisation matrix in Excel
Repeating the same sample request every year
today.time_sinks: Time goes to collecting evidence across three sites and to samples that turn out to be ordinary, not to the few control gaps that matter.

lenses.faster: The sample, the authorisation report and the list of late journals are ready before the review. The accountant spends the meeting on the gaps.
lenses.autonomous: Once a month a control report runs: users who can both enter and pay, journals after lock, suspense older than 30 days, and new suppliers created and paid in the same week.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would run these checks every night and hand the auditor a query instead of a once-a-year file.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses collecting screenshots. The useful part is deciding which gap is a real risk in a warehouse operation.
lenses.options: Several samples are prepared: random, high-amount, new supplier, and manual journal. The accountant chooses which one the auditor will see.
lenses.altitude: The accountant designs the tests and the thresholds. The monthly run is the system, not a personal checklist.
reach: Parts of the Controller's internal-control file
Authorisation reviews the Finance Director is asked to sign
Procedure checks the bookkeepers currently answer ad hoc

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a break is a control failure or a sensible workaround, and what to change in AFAS afterwards.
tasks.pattern_why: The tests can be drafted and the evidence pulled automatically, but the inspection judgment stays with the accountant. This is review work, not a posting.

in_practice.trigger: The monthly control calendar, an auditor PBC list, or a change in AFAS authorisations.
steps: Run the fixed tests against the AFAS log and the nightly extract.
Draft a short finding for each break, with the posting, the user and the procedure it sits against.
The accountant marks each finding as gap, accepted workaround, or false alarm.
Agreed actions are written to the Controller, with an owner and a date.
The sample and the sign-off are filed for the auditor.
in_practice.human_gate: No finding is sent to the auditor or used to change a procedure until the accountant has classified it. The Controller agrees any change to who may pay or post.
systems: AFAS Profit authorisation and audit log
data_needed: AFAS user rights for enter, approve, pay and master data
Journal log with user, time and period
Written procedures the tests refer to
Last year's auditor findings
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint control folder, separate from any personal HR file.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit records user rights and keeps a log of postings and workflow steps.
MindBridge reviews general-ledger entries for unusual combinations.
A monthly rules report on segregation, late journals and old suspense can be written on the AFAS extract without a model.

risks: A report that ranks or times individual bookkeepers can be a personnel-monitoring system and needs works council consent before it is introduced.
Under the EU AI Act, using a model to allocate work or assess people in employment is a different, heavier use than checking ledger rules.
An anomaly model will flag seasonal flex peaks and site reclasses as suspicious and bury the real breaks.
False comfort: a green report is not evidence if the underlying AFAS log is incomplete.
research_questions: Does AFAS already produce an authorisation report that shows who can enter, approve and pay, and is anyone reviewing it?
Does the external auditor rely on AFAS application controls, or on samples pulled by hand?
Which procedures are on SharePoint, and which exist only with the two accountants?
Would the works council treat a named-user control report as a monitoring system that needs consent?

today.trigger: The close checklist reaches accruals, prepayments, depreciation, cut-off and reclasses.
steps: List recurring journals from last month and drop the ones that should reverse.
Calculate flex-labour accrual, received-not-invoiced transport and warehouse cost, and prepaid release.
Take depreciation and payroll journals from AFAS where the modules already post them.
Type the memoriaal in AFAS with a description and a reversal date.
The Controller reviews material lines before the period locks.
drudgery: Re-keying the same prepaid and depreciation amounts
Copying last month's accrual and changing one number
Writing the same journal description twelve times a year
today.time_sinks: The judgmental accruals take the time: flex hours not yet invoiced, trips without a proof of delivery, and energy and rent bills that arrive after close.

lenses.faster: Recurring journals are proposed from the AFAS schedule with amount, account, site and reversal date filled in. The accountant edits only the lines that changed.
lenses.autonomous: On the accrual day the proposal is created from open receipts, the prepaid schedule and the approved agency hours. It waits in the queue. It does not wait for a reminder.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would accrue flex labour and delivered-not-invoiced transport every week, so the forecast does not jump on close day.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses typing the standing journals. Choosing the flex accrual and the cut-off is the work that still needs an accountant.
lenses.options: The flex accrual is shown at ordered hours, at approved hours, and at last month's run-rate, with the effect on each site's result.
lenses.altitude: The accountant keeps the accrual methods and the materiality rules. The schedule produces the standard journals.
reach: The payroll journal check shared with the payroll specialist
Holiday-allowance and CAO accrual review on the general ledger
The actuals side of the FP&A bridge for cost that is not invoiced yet

tasks.human_edge: Setting the amount when the source is incomplete, and refusing a journal that would make a site result look finished when it is not.
tasks.pattern_why: The amounts must come from a source schedule, not from a model guess, and a journal must not hit the official books until the accountant approves it.

in_practice.trigger: The close calendar reaches accrual day, or a weekly file of approved agency hours and open receipts arrives.
steps: Calculate each recurring journal from its source: prepaid schedule, asset module, open receipts, or agency hours times agreed rate minus invoices already posted.
Propose the memoriaal with accounts, kostenplaats, description and reversal date.
Show the movement versus last month and versus the forecast.
The accountant changes or accepts each material line.
AFAS posts only the accepted lines and reverses the ones marked as reversing.
in_practice.human_gate: Nothing posts without the accountant's approval. A line with no source balance cannot be proposed. Amounts above the Controller's materiality need the Controller as well.
data_needed: Prepaid and accrual schedule with contra accounts
Open goods-received-not-invoiced and trips without POD
Agency hours approved, by site and rate
Materiality set by the Controller
CAO and payroll figures for holiday allowance already posted by payroll
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS journal log, with the source file and the approver stored in the SharePoint close folder.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports memoriaal entries and recurring periodic bookings.
AFAS Payroll can post its journal into AFAS Profit financials.
FloQast supports close checklists and review of journal entries before they are treated as final.
A flex accrual can be computed as approved hours times the agreed rate, minus invoices already in AFAS, when the agency file is complete.

risks: A model that fills a missing accrual with a plausible number will create a false site result. The amount has to be computed from a named source.
Double accrual is likely where AFAS Payroll already posts holiday allowance under the CAO and the accountant also books it.
Posting a weekly flex accrual from personal data in agency files has to stay inside AFAS under AVG.
If operations cannot confirm hours or POD by the accrual day, faster journals only mean faster wrong journals.
research_questions: Which journals are already recurring in AFAS, and which are still typed from Excel each month?
Is there a reliable received-not-invoiced balance for transport and warehouse purchases?
Do approved agency hours arrive in time to accrue by site, or only as a monthly invoice after close?
What amount does the Controller allow a standing journal to post with only a schedule check?

tasks.short: Keep the bookkeepers' close work moving and complete.

today.trigger: The close calendar, a missing file, or a deadline for the VAT return, the auditor or the Rabobank batch.
steps: Tell the three bookkeepers which files, codings and reconciliations are due.
Check what has been posted and what is still open across the three sites.
Chase late items by Teams or mail.
Collect the pack that has to be sent to the auditor, the Belastingdienst filing or the bank.
Confirm to the Controller that the file is complete.
drudgery: Status meetings that only collect dates
Repeating the same chase mail every month
Maintaining a close tracker that is already out of date
today.time_sinks: The time is the chasing and the rework when a file arrives incomplete, not the decision about what the close contains.

lenses.faster: The status of every close task is visible without asking. The accountant steps in only when a task is blocked or late.
lenses.autonomous: On the due day the checklist reminds the owner, then the accountant, then the Controller. Official files are assembled when the required tasks are green.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the close calendar would cover bookkeepers, payroll and the three site administrators, and the month would have a known critical path.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the chase mail. The part worth keeping is helping a bookkeeper through a real blockage and signing a file that is actually complete.
lenses.options: The accountant sees two or three close sequences, for example a fast close that defers non-material sites and a full close, with the day each would finish.
lenses.altitude: The accountant designs the calendar, the owners and the definition of done. The checklist does the reminding.
reach: Close coordination the Controller now does by mail
VAT filing readiness shared with the bookkeepers
The list of audit requests the Finance Director is chased for

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what slips, what blocks the close, and how to deal with a person whose work is not good enough.
tasks.pattern_why: Reminders, status and file assembly can run from a checklist. Sending a VAT return, an audit file or a payment batch still needs a named person.

in_practice.trigger: The close calendar opens the period, or a required task passes its due time.
steps: Publish the task list with owner, due day and the AFAS or SharePoint evidence that closes it.
Send a reminder to the owner on the due day. Escalate to the accountant only when the due time is missed.
Block the official pack while a required task is open.
Assemble the VAT support, the reconciliation folder and the auditor folder from the closed tasks.
The accountant releases the pack, or agrees a dated exception with the Controller.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant decides priority and any exception to the calendar. A person still authorises the VAT filing, the audit file and the bank batch. The system must not score or rank employees.
data_needed: Close calendar with owner and definition of done
AFAS task or posting status
List of statutory sends: VAT return, Rabobank batch, auditor file, Kamer van Koophandel when relevant
in_practice.logs_to: The close checklist history in SharePoint, showing due time, finish time and who released the pack.

evidence.claim: FloQast and Trintech Cadency keep a close checklist with owners, due dates and status.
AFAS Profit workflow can assign a task and record that it was finished.
A system that monitors how individual employees work can require works council consent under the Dutch Works Councils Act before it is introduced.

risks: Automated chasing that records speed per bookkeeper is a works council matter and an AVG matter. Task status is enough.
The EU AI Act treats systems that assess or allocate work to people more strictly than a checklist of files.
A green status can mean the box was ticked, not that the reconciliation was any good.
Reminders to payroll and the sites fail if those teams never agreed the calendar.
research_questions: Is there a written close calendar with an owner and a due day, or does it sit with the two accountants?
How many hours a month go to chasing status rather than reviewing the work?
Will the bookkeepers and the works council accept automated reminders if the system does not score people?
Which sends are mandatory (VAT, bank batch, auditor, Kamer van Koophandel), and who must authorise each today?

tasks.short: Maintain the chart of accounts and code entries to it.

today.trigger: A new supplier, a new cost type, a site question, or a line the bookkeepers cannot code.
steps: Decide whether an existing grootboekrekening, btw-code and kostenplaats fit.
Open a new account only when the Controller agrees it is needed.
Tell the bookkeepers the default coding for that supplier.
Update the Excel mapping that feeds Power BI.
Correct coding errors found at close.
drudgery: Answering the same supplier-coding question again
Fixing lines coded to a suspense account
Updating the Power BI mapping by hand after an account is added
today.time_sinks: Repeated coding questions and the repair of wrong VAT or wrong site take more time than opening new accounts.

lenses.faster: Known suppliers are coded from an approved default. Only new suppliers and low-confidence lines come to the accountant.
lenses.autonomous: A new supplier or an uncoded line opens a coding task on its own. The Power BI mapping updates when a new account is approved, not at the next close.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the chart would show warehouse, transport and overhead by site all year, stable enough that the forecast and the actuals use the same dimensions.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the repeat coding questions. Designing a chart that operations can read is the part worth doing.
lenses.options: For a new cost, the accountant sees two or three existing accounts it could use before anyone opens a new one.
lenses.altitude: The accountant governs the chart, the VAT defaults and the dimension rules. Day-to-day coding follows those rules.
reach: Default coding the bookkeepers now ask about
The dimension definitions FP&A needs for the forecast
The payroll cost-centre mapping shared with the payroll specialist

tasks.human_edge: Deciding that a new account is justified, and choosing the VAT treatment for a transport flow the master data has not seen before.
tasks.pattern_why: Invoice text and supplier history are unstructured input. The output is a structured account, VAT code and cost centre, and AFAS can reject any code that is not in the chart.

in_practice.trigger: A new supplier is created, or a line arrives without a default account.
steps: Propose grootboek, btw-code and kostenplaats from the supplier default and, if there is none, from the invoice text and similar suppliers.
Accept the proposal only when every code already exists in AFAS.
Auto-apply the coding once the accountant has approved that supplier rule.
Queue new accounts, new VAT treatments and low-confidence lines.
When a new account is approved, add it to the Power BI mapping before anyone posts to it.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves every new account and every new VAT treatment. The Controller approves a change to the chart structure. Repeat coding uses only rules already approved.
data_needed: Current grootboekschema, btw-codes and kostenplaatsen
Supplier defaults and the last year of posted lines
Power BI mapping file
Written VAT positions for domestic, reverse-charge and zero-rated transport
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS supplier rule and a chart-change log on SharePoint, including who approved a new account.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit holds the chart of accounts, VAT codes and cost centres, and can store a default account on a supplier.
Invoice-capture products propose a general-ledger account from supplier history and invoice text, and a person can restrict the choice to existing accounts.
International transport often uses a zero rate or the Dutch reverse charge, and that choice changes the VAT return.

risks: A suggested btw-code that is merely plausible will misstate the VAT return. New treatments stay with the accountant.
Opening accounts freely will break history and the Power BI pack the forecast depends on.
Auto-coding into a suspense account hides the problem until close and adds audit adjustments.
Supplier invoices can contain personal data of flex workers. The suggestion step should read the commercial line, not build a profile of a person.
research_questions: How many new general-ledger accounts were opened in the last year, and who approved them?
What share of lines is coded from a supplier default, and what share is decided line by line?
Does a new account or kostenplaats break Power BI until someone edits a mapping file?
How often is the VAT code on a logistics invoice different from the supplier master?

tasks.short: Change and document how the accounting system works.

today.trigger: A close pain, a new agency feed, an auditor remark, or a Power BI report that no longer matches AFAS.
steps: Describe the current path from source document to ledger to dashboard.
Agree the change with the Controller, and with the external AFAS consultant when configuration is involved.
Adjust AFAS workflows, journals or dimensions, and the Excel files around them.
Rewrite the procedure on SharePoint.
Check the next close to see whether the change held.
drudgery: Writing procedures that repeat what the screens already do
Keeping a private Excel because the interface was never finished
Explaining the same workaround to each new bookkeeper
today.time_sinks: The slow part is unspecified interfaces: agency hours, bank files and the nightly extract, plus documentation that is older than the system.

lenses.faster: A draft of the process note, the control points and the test cases is ready from the current AFAS setup. The accountant edits the design instead of starting from a blank page.
lenses.autonomous: A failed interface or a mapping break opens a change task with the last successful run attached. The documentation date is checked when the related close task runs.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost finance would have one documented path from each agency and from Rabobank into AFAS and Power BI, and would retire the side Excel files.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rewriting screen-shots after every small AFAS change. The good work is choosing a simpler process and seeing the next close get shorter.
lenses.options: Two or three designs are compared for a change, for example a supplier default, a new dimension, or a weekly accrual file, with the close-day effect of each.
lenses.altitude: This task is already the system layer. The shift is to spend the hours on design and test, not on manual patches between systems.
reach: Data definitions the FP&A analysts need from the ledger
The payroll-to-ledger interface shared with the payroll specialist and the HRIS analyst
Bookkeeper work instructions that today are passed on verbally

tasks.human_edge: Choosing a design that the auditor can test, that the bookkeepers will actually use, and that does not weaken segregation of duties.
tasks.pattern_why: Drafting the note, the test and the specification can be assisted. Changing AFAS, and deciding what the system of record is, stays with the accountant and the Controller.

in_practice.trigger: A close retrospective, a broken feed, an auditor finding, or a new report the business asks for.
steps: Describe the current flow, the manual patches and the control gaps, using the AFAS log and the SharePoint manual.
Draft two or three options with what would post, who would approve, and how the auditor would reperform it.
The accountant and the Controller pick one option.
Specify the AFAS change or the file layout, and draft the procedure and the test.
After the next close, compare days to close and the number of manual journals with the month before.
in_practice.human_gate: No AFAS configuration, authorisation or interface goes live without the accountant and the Controller. A consultant may build it. The accountant accepts the test.
data_needed: Current process notes and the AFAS configuration they refer to
Close timings and counts of manual journals
File layouts from Rabobank and the agencies
Authorisation matrix
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint change log: decision, test result, who approved, and the close month it first affected.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot drafts and rewrites procedure text from documents stored in SharePoint.
AFAS Profit finance configuration is administered as a setup change, separate from posting entries.
A coding assistant can draft a SQL check or a Power BI measure, and a person can test it on the nightly extract.

risks: A generated procedure that does not match the live AFAS setup will be worse than no procedure, because the auditor may rely on it.
Giving an assistant write access to AFAS configuration can bypass segregation of duties.
Building a side database of invoices or hours outside AFAS creates a second ledger and an AVG processor question.
Works council consent belongs in the design if the new system records how individual staff complete administrative tasks.
research_questions: Who is allowed to change AFAS finance configuration today, the accountant or an external consultant?
Which records still move through Excel because AFAS cannot take them, especially agency hours, claims and energy?
Is the SharePoint accounting manual current with the live workflows?
What evidence would the external auditor want before relying on a finance-owned feed into the ledger?

role.altitude: The accountant stops being the person who re-keys, ties out and chases, and becomes the owner of the close design: the coding rules, the reconciliation tolerances, the accrual methods and the checks that make the monthly figures something the business will not reopen.
reach: Straight-through purchase-invoice coding and payment proposals that the bookkeepers now process by hand
Customer cash matching shared with the credit and collections officer, using the same Rabobank file
The payroll and holiday-allowance tie-out to the ledger, shared with the payroll specialist, without taking over payslips
The first draft of the Controller's management pack and control file
The actuals side of the FP&A bridge, so the forecast starts from a ledger the analysts do not rebuild
role.ceiling_note: Two accountants are about 3,200 hours a year at a loaded cost of EUR 70. These eight tasks are roughly two fifths of that. Hours come out only where AFAS master data, Rabobank references and the three agency files are good. A bad file turns coding time into exception time and saves little. The role cannot absorb the Controller's signature, the commercial forecast, or credit decisions on customers. Official sends, including VAT, the annual accounts and bank batches, stay with a named person. A system that scores the bookkeepers needs the works council before it is switched on.
skills_to_grow: AFAS close design and the authorisation split between proposing a posting and releasing a Rabobank batch
Dutch GAAP and the VAT treatments for warehousing and transport, written as rules a test can check
Reconciliation design and audit evidence: match keys, tolerances and a log the auditor can reperform
Reading the nightly Power BI extract well enough to retire the Excel bridges, and knowing when it is a day behind the ledger
Enough SQL or AFAS GetConnector skill to specify a check without waiting for a consultant
role.ambitious_version: The month closes in a few days because every standing accrual, bank line, supplier code and subledger tie-out has either posted under a rule or arrived as a named exception. The two accountants spend the remaining time on cut-off at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, on whether the forecast starts from figures the business will stand behind, and on a control file the auditor can test without a fire drill.
